description: The image presents a four-quadrant circular diagram, visually structured like a pie chart divided into four equal 90-degree segments, each representing a distinct category of evaluation criteria for reasoning benchmarks in large language models (LLMs). The top-left quadrant, colored yellow, is labeled “Complexity” and associated with the term “Uncrushable,” accompanied by a ladder icon, suggesting hierarchical or layered difficulty. The top-right quadrant, in light blue, is labeled “Instance” and paired with “Unhackable,” featuring a shield icon with a checkmark, implying robustness against adversarial manipulation. The bottom-left quadrant, in red, is labeled “Scalable Oversight” and linked to “Auto-verifiable,” with a clipboard-and-checkmark icon, indicating the capacity for automated validation at scale. The bottom-right quadrant, in green, is labeled “Coverage” and associated with “General,” illustrated with a globe-and-gear icon, denoting broad applicability across domains. Each quadrant is visually emphasized with a corresponding colored callout box containing its associated descriptor, reinforcing the conceptual mapping between the core category and its defining attribute. The overall layout suggests a balanced, multi-dimensional framework for assessing LLM reasoning capabilities, with each axis contributing an equally weighted dimension to the evaluation space.
